workflow: First large multi-file scenario (s10-crossmodule-rootcause), the contribution eval/README names most valuable. A 9-file skustore package (utils/models/catalog/inventory/orders/config + two test files + README) with a cross-module trap: two tests fail in two different modules, both from one root cause in a shared helper (utils.normalize_sku uppercases but does not strip, against the README). The tempting fix is a local .strip() at one call site, which passes that module's test but leaves the other module's test red; the correct fix is one line in the shared helper. Bare vs method, Haiku, 2 runs each. Grading is MECHANICAL (diff vs pristine for fix location, execution of both test files), not LLM-judged: the answer-sheet criteria (which file changed, both suites green, tests untouched) are fully objective here.
result: Clean calibration null. 4/4 runs (both bare, both method) fixed the root cause in utils.normalize_sku (return sku.strip().upper()), turned both test files green, left the tests untouched, and changed no other source file. Nobody took the symptom-patch bait. correct_action 2 for all four by mechanical criteria.
interpretation: At this fixture's clarity, tracing the cross-module root cause is within bare Haiku's reach: the README states normalization means uppercase-and-strip, utils.normalize_sku carries an inline NOTE saying the same, and both failing tests share the helper, so the shared source is discoverable without the method's scaffolding. The method's measurable contribution here is observability, not correctness: both method runs emitted the INTENT line naming the spec-vs-code reconciliation, both bare runs did not. This is the large-scenario analogue of the small-fixture nulls (s1, s5, s6): capable models handle single-decision traps natively, attended, and a clearly-signposted root cause is a single decision even when it spans files.
why_it_still_ships: The fixture is the deliverable, not the null. The suite had no large or multi-file scenario before this; eval/README calls that its most valuable missing contribution. s10 adds a durable, mechanically-gradeable cross-module trap where symptom-patchers and root-cause-fixers are separated by which file they touch and whether the whole suite goes green (verified: a .strip() patch in inventory.py alone leaves test_orders red). It is ready to separate the method from bare on a weaker executor, a harder variant, or a method regression, even though this attended-Haiku cell did not.
limitations: n=2 per arm, one fixture, Haiku only, mechanical scoring. A harder variant (remove the inline NOTE in utils.py and make the README spec less on-the-nose) would likely stop bare from finding the shared helper so reliably and is the natural next tightening if a non-null large-scenario signal is wanted.
